If you stray too far outside of the lines you'll still put down paint though, so no cheating!

notes.title: Eye dropper & more!
notes.notes:
It's time for a few cool new features!

[list]
[*]Vermillion now features an eye dropper. Press and hold the former clean brush button (the lower button on your brush hand controller) to pick any color from the canvas, palette, mixing tray or rag. Aim into empty space to clear the brush.
[*]Paint blobs on the palette now resist mixing so you don't have to clean your brush before sampling another color on the palette.
[*]Paint blobs on the palette are bigger.
[*]You now get a posed ghost hand to hold the brush.
[*]The laser pointer is stabilized to make it much easier to click things.
[*]The laser pointer is now always following the direction of your controller, rather than the brush.
[*]Fixed hand stabilizer ruler not rotating properly depending on how the easel is facing.
[*]Fixed palette and brush stand being in the wrong position when changing handedness with the easel at a non standard orientation.
[*]Web pages can now be dragged to scroll them.
[/list]

As always, if you're enjoying Vermillion, please consider leaving a review. Thanks for your continued support!

notes.title: Fixed screen stuck in floor
notes.notes: This patch should fix the floating screen being stuck in the floor. Apologies!

notes.title: Easier easel movement!
notes.notes: The easel has always been a bit clunky to move. No more! You can now move the easel in all dimensions with just one grip, and easily and swiftly position it anywhere you like. I've also opened up the entire studio floor for you to position the easel in, as this feature has often been requested. Now you can see the studios from entirely new angles!

notes.title: Built-in paint by numbers pack & more
notes.notes:
No idea what to paint? Vermillion now comes with its first paint by numbers pack, giving you the choice of four pre-made PBN templates to get started straight away. You can of course still generate PBN templates from your own images. [b]The generator panel has moved to the new Paint by numbers page on the floating screen, under the Custom tab.[/b]

Additional changes:
[list]
[*]The tutorial now skips the palette undo action, and instead the button binding is shown on a foldout panel on the palette.
[*]The tutorial now has clear calls to action on every step, to avoid any confusion on what is expected.
[/list]

notes.title: Paint by numbers update!
notes.notes:
You can now generate a paint by numbers template from your own images and any image you find online! Vermillion will generate the outlines, which you can show above or below the paint on the canvas. The palette will be automatically filled with the required colors, between 2 and 20. You can change how detailed you want the outlines to be. You can isolate outlines to one color at a time, so you can very easily apply the right color in the right area. Painting has never been more accessible! 

Additionally, you can now open local images on the floating screen directly from inside Vermillion, which you can also use to generate paint by numbers templates.

As always, if you're enjoying the update, please consider leaving a review! Greatly appreciated. Have fun! 🙏🏻

notes.title: Gallery & Glossy paint update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, I've been hard at work on the Quest MR update, and I'm passing the savings onto [i]you[/i]! 

[list]
[*]You can now mount your paintings in the Manor and Loft studios by approaching a wall, and even have them sitting in a customizable frame.
[*]The paint now looks a whole lot glossier. It's pretty damn tasty if you ask me. You can still reduce or disable the specular highlight using the slider on the lamp, but will you want to? I think not.
[*]The painting settings have moved to a little panel on the palette, where you can now set the canvas mixing sensitivity, paint thickness, and an all new infinite paint toggle. I've revamped the canvas mixing sensitivity at 0 to properly never mix with what was on the canvas. With the mixing sensitivity at 0 and the infinite paint toggle enabled you can doodle away at your heart's content!
[*]You can grab anything from a distance now, so you don't have to reach and stretch or bump into the real world.
[*]I've fixed the hands being the wrong way around if you're starting in OpenVR as a leftie. Sorry about that!
[*]I've changed the two inch brush to have a smoother look to its paint. 
[*]A dry palette knife is now an excellent tool for smoothing paint on the canvas. Try it, it's something else.
[/list]

If you're enjoying the update, please leave a store review! That really helps out. Thanks!

notes.title: Overlay, Locomotion, Outdoor studio & OpenVR update
notes.notes:
The overlay is now out of beta! Have fun painting in any VR game. Remember that you need a powerful system to run two VR games simultaneously. You can always lower the SteamVR render resolution to gain performance!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=udc1i97KPLY

Another important change this update brings is improved locomotion. Locomotion was always a second class citizen in Vermillion, but this is no longer the case.
[list]
[*]Better teleport
[*]Smooth locomotion
[*]Snap, quick, and smooth rotation
[*]Grab locomotion (very useful to position yourself just right!)
[/list]
The smooth locomotion options are especially useful in overlay mode!

One more cool addition this update brings is a new outdoor studio. You know, in case you're done painting in Skyrim or VRChat.

The final important change this update brings is that now the default VR runtime is OpenVR, instead of OpenXR. OpenXR is the supposed new standard, but it's been nothing but trouble since Vermillion's launch. To this day it causes some users' controllers to not track. Out with the new, in with the old! You can still use the OpenXR launch option to bypass SteamVR on non-SteamVR platforms, such as Oculus and WMR.

Artwork by @lizaledwards!

notes.notes:
Ever dreamed of painting the mountains of Skyrim? Or sit on the balcony overlooking City 17 while doodling away? You can now, using the overlay beta. It renders Vermillion as an overlay over any Steam VR game. It captures the inputs, so there's no interference. You can turn the input capture on/off easily with a toggle at your feet, where you can also hide the overlay entirely.

To opt into the beta, right click Vermillion in your Steam library > Betas > select [b]overlay[/b]. You now get a new launch option to start Vermillion as an overlay. I'm really looking forward to see where you will be painting!

Artwork by the talented Liz Edwards! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vArWTlRieGI

notes.title: Major layer improvements!
notes.notes:
You requested it, and here it is!

[list]
[*]You can now merge layers down. This allows you to free up layers, so you can make complex compositions without worry.
[*]You can now move layers. Gone are the days of forgetting to start on layer 2, and not being able to put in your background afterwards.
[*]The longest standing bug in Vermillion is fixed: blurring a paint stroke on a higher layer no longer creates a white halo.
[/list]
Note that you can only merge layers on new paintings. This is because the way transparent paint used to be shown on the canvas was incorrect, and made it impossible to merge layers down. Your old paintings are not affected by this change, but you therefore also can't merge layers on those.

Other changes:

[list]
[*]You now see the player names above their heads when you're on the multiplayer session page, so you can easily block or mute the right person.
[*]I scaled the Facebook avatar heads down to make them human-sized. 
[*]Fixed spots of opaque paint appearing in the stroke of the dagger brush with thinned paint.
[*]Fixed the floating screen lagging behind the item it's docked to.
[/list]

notes.title: System default OpenXR launch option and more
notes.notes:
When you're launching Vermillion now, you get the choice between a regular launch, and launching with the system default OpenXR. If you've been running Vermillion fine so far and you have no idea what an OpenXR is, then feel free to move on to the change list. If Vermillion has not launched in VR for you, for instance if you have the Varjo Aero, then read on after the list.

[list]
[*]Fixed premade paintings not copying. If you recently got Vermillion, now you'll get the default paintings (toucan etc).
[*]Browser resolution is slightly higher, so you have more space on the web pages.
[*]Added "Show UI" option for the spectator camera.
[*]Fixed error when launching with LIV.
[*]Fixed projector alpha arrow being yellow.
[/list]

So, OpenXR. OpenXR is the standard for VR and AR applications, defined by all the big players in the space. Every company creating VR hardware has created their own runtime, so that their hardware can run VR applications through OpenXR. Valve is the only one that supports all other headsets, with SteamVR OpenXR. Vermillion chooses this by default, because it's the one that's most likely to work, especially if you have headsets of different manufacturers. However, in some cases it doesn't, like I'm hearing now with the Varjo Aero. In this case, you need to use the OpenXR runtime of that specific VR vendor. In the application that comes with your VR headset (i.e. the Oculus desktop tool, the WMR portal, the Varjo tool, the Vive tool, or SteamVR), you can set the system default OpenXR runtime to that platform. Once you've done that, run Vermillion in System default OpenXR mode.

notes.notes:
I'm currently working on adding Steam Workshop support for custom environments, and I figured I'd give you all a heads up in case you want to start chipping away on a personal studio or even outdoor environment you'd want to paint in. You will just have to deliver the environment as a single .glb file, in which all the models and textures are defined. You will also be able to supply your own skybox and ambience. Just modelling & texturing in Blender, and exporting as a .glb, will work perfectly. Be sure to bake the lighting as well, as there is no real time lighting in Vermillion. 

You can get the template file [url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1N_y56WXbTqM9MEuFfDYt5U1PGOflL6ww]here[/url] which shows where the easel goes and which direction it's facing.

notes.title: The Big Update
notes.notes:
The big update is live! These are all the changes I've been working on the past months for the Quest release. 

[list]
[*]The painting mechanics have been improved, removing common artifacts while painting.
[*]The paint thinner has been improved. Note that paint can no longer be thickened up again by adding opaque paint on the palette, to make it easier to maintain a constant opacity. You can add more thinner by loading more thinner from the bucket and going back to the palette.
[*]There's a completely new easel, which is far more flexible. It can be folded flat so you can rest your hand on a table, or even turned upside down so you can paint lying down. There's a new grip on the mixing tray as well, allowing you to move and rotate the entire easel, making it easier to get it just right instead of having to rely on teleporting.
[*]The brushes, brush and palette stand had a makeover.
[*]There's two new brushes: a dagger brush (both smooth and rough variants), and a silicone dagger color shaper, both scalable. Try using the latter to move paint around on the canvas!
[*]The short flat brushes are now fully scalable.
[*]The rag now has a single tip, and has pressure based wiping. Dip the rag in paint thinner to fully erase paint.
[*]The palette knife now needs to be tilted to create the stipple pattern, rather than it being pressure based.
[*]Added a lamp on the easel, with which you can turn off the glare on the canvas.
[*]The Manor studio has been refurbished.
[*]A new studio has been added, a whitewall loft.
[*]Vermillion is now localized in German, Spanish, Italian, French, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese, Japanese and Korean.
[*]You now have 20 canvas undos instead of 5. The undos are also a lot more granular, happening after every slight change instead of grouping several daubs together.
[*]The palette and mixing tray are saved alongside the painting, so you can always get back to painting without having to remix colors.
[*]Paint on the palette is glossier, removing the glare, and looking quite shiny at the right angle.
[*]New web browser.
[/list]

Bug fixes:
[list]
[*]The correct OpenXR runtime is now chosen behind the scenes, instead of making you do it.
[*]Fixed LIV not teleporting correctly.
[*]Made it easier to beat the devil out of the brushes.
[/list]

Since this is a major update, it's not unlikely that there's some issues. Let me know on the forums or on Discord if you run into any problems! https://vermillion-vr.com/discord

notes.title: LIV support, optimization and impasto improvements.
notes.notes:
Vermillion now has LIV support! Excited to see what the content creators will cook up. Besides that, there's a bunch of nice fixes in this update:

- Added optimization on palette and mixing tray, which should alleviate performance issues for users who had issues with those surfaces but not the canvas.
- Fine tuned the paint thickness output of several brushes.
- When touching thick paint with a dry brush, you now leave that brush's bristly texture in the thick paint, rather than flattening it completely from the start. Play around with it, it's good fun.
- The hands when not holding a tool are now animated.
- Fixed blobs appearing in 2 inch brush strokes.
- Adjusted paint visual on brush tips to show full paint more clearly.
- Fixed 2 inch brush tip showing more paint than it should.
- Adding straight paint thinner to the palette will now always thin the paint further.
- Removed sounds from small synthetic brushes which were a bit off.
- Fixed save directory thumbnail not showing latest save.

[b]Oculus branch only:[/b]

- Audio is redirected to device selected in Oculus app (i.e. the Oculus HMD or the Windows default device)
- Dash is supported
- Game pauses when taking off the headset

notes.title: Small fixes before I leave on vacation!
notes.notes:
I'm AFK for a week, so I wanted to make sure I leave things properly before I head out.

- Paint applied on the canvas will now blend less when going over top of thinned paint (e.g. when you've made "liquid white" by mixing white and paint thinner, and applied it to the canvas). Use straight up white if you prefer the strong blend as it was before.
- Adjust tutorial to go into further detail about the thick paint. It's a good idea to restart the tutorial from the settings in case you're struggling.
- Fixed some errors.

notes.title: The Impasto Update + G2 support
notes.notes:
Impasto? Yeah, I could eat. Or rather, impasto is the effect of using very thick paint on the canvas to create a textured look. I have updated the paint visuals to be much thicker, giving you the option to create rich texture on your canvas. If you like to keep it flat, you can always use less paint, flatten the thick paint with any tool, or use the slider in Settings > Painting. While this in itself is a great new feature, the main driver behind it was the ability for achieving better Bob Ross style foliage - i.e. tapping in happy little bushes. The two inch brush is now rounded, the one inch oval brush doesn't leave a circle mark, and tapping in leaves and bushes gives you a very nice textured look, rather than the sort of rectangular muddiness you've had up to now when using the 2 inch. Try tapping in leaves with a fully loaded 2 inch (look at the pressure indicator) to see what I mean!

Your old paintings will not automatically show thicker paint. You can scale it up in the settings.

Additional changes:

- Reverb G2 controllers are now functional in the base Steam version, without having to switch to the system default OpenXR branch.
- Bristle (rough) variant of the one inch oval brush.
- Classic fan brush is back, since it allows smoother blending on things such as skin.
- Clicking a save thumbnail does not automatically open the last save, but shows all thumbnails instead.
- Palette knife scratching strength reduced again to what it was before last update.
- Fixed some brushes not being able to paint over some parts of the canvas.
- Several smaller bug fixes.

notes.title: The Crimson Update
notes.notes:
By popular request, I've made the default palette the complete Bob Ross landscape colors set.

I have adjusted the color model to allow for darker reds - this change will only happen in new paintings. Your old paintings are unaffected.

When using higher pressure with the 2 inch, the bristly pattern is no longer visible, allowing for smoother blends.

Improved the fan brush pattern to be more bristly, so it should be easier to get natural looking pine trees.

Added censored mode for the browser for spectators.

The brush sounds now fade out smoothly rather than cutting off harshly when no longer making contact with a surface / paint thinner.

Fixed the rag being able to load paint thinner. Shoutout to Harrier for reporting this!

I have removed the ticking sound for the spectator camera UI, since it was distracting when mixing paint on the canvas.

This is now fixed. Please, remove your old custom palettes. Sorry for the inconvenience! Shoutout to Vermillion user Woycraft for pointing this out to me.

I also made palette saving asynchronous, so there is no longer a small hitch when saving a custom palette.

notes.title: Performance mode for lower end hardware
notes.notes:
There's now a setting to halve the resolution of all paintable surfaces (palette, canvas and mixing tray). You will be offered the option to switch when first learning about the palette in the tutorial. You can also switch at any time in the settings. Use the low resolution mode if you are experiencing performance issues when touching the brush to these surfaces.

Additional changes:
- Cleaned up the UI a bit

[b]IMPORTANT NOTE TO COSMOS OWNERS:[/b]

I am aware that currently, Cosmos controllers are not tracking. The issues lies with Unity and HTC not being on top of their OpenXR game. There is an unofficial patch for this, but I just tried it now and it actually broke the entire build. I will try to work with HTC and Unity to get this resolved ASAP!
